body: Review-and-fix pass over the current head (a1b19bd0e), together with web-platform-tests/wpt#64904. ### Questions / follow-ups - **Firefox applies `img sizes=auto` even when the selected `` has its own `sizes`.** In Firefox, `` selects the `auto` width (10px) rather than the 300px from `` (first assertion of the "Removing sizes from ``" subtest). The spec (before and after this PR) says the `source`'s `sizes` wins, so this looks like a Gecko bug rather than a spec question, but it's worth confirming with Gecko folks and filing. - Firefox also accepts ` auto` on `` (resolves it instead of rejecting the entry) and treats an explicit empty `` as `auto` rather than `100vw`. Both are the leniencies this PR deliberately does *not* bless, so they are implementation gaps, not test issues. Chrome Canary passes all 11 subtests. ### Findings 1. **Dropped the only explicit statement that an `img`'s own `sizes=auto` is matched literally** (editorial, fixed in 1dfc97e10). The removed sentence ("the entire `` value must either be the string "auto" or start with "auto,"") was too strict for ``, where the new grammar (and the parser, see the `/*comment*/auto` tests) is the right constraint. But for the `img` element itself that literal requirement still exists: it's what `allows auto-sizes` checks, and the authoring conditions require `allows auto-sizes`. Readers of the grammar won't see that, so I added a note under the authoring conditions pointing it out, contrasting it with ``. No normative change; the restriction was already there via `allows auto-sizes`, which also matches Chromium's `HTMLImageElement::AllowAutoSizes`. Checked and found no issue: every entry's whitespace/empty handling, the `(mc) auto` rejection path, non-first `auto` leniency note vs algorithm, the null-`sizes` (omitted ``) fallback through `create a source set`, the Link header call site (`img` = null), and `check_algorithms.py` / `check_wpt_coverage.py` (only pre-existing noise). Build passes.

Open: Q1. Not applied: D1. New in this review: Q1: When a `source` omits `sizes` and the `img` allows auto-sizes, should the `source` use a bare `auto` (as in this PR) or the `img`'s own `sizes` value? They differ when `auto` can't be resolved yet. Take `` before the `img` is rendered; with scripting disabled, it's fetched at that point. A bare `auto` gives 100vw, while the `img`'s value gives 300px. - a. Keep as is (bare `auto`). This matches Chromium and Gecko, and what #8008 specified and #9493's note ("equivalent to specifying auto") still says. The `img`'s fallback entries don't apply to the `source`. - b. Use the `img`'s `sizes` value, so the author's fallback applies when `auto` can't be resolved. This matches WebKit in this case. Prototype: [spec](https://github.com/zcorpan/html/commit/532d6b9d0ec71ca28f9797ef315afadb0e9772c5), [test](https://github.com/zcorpan/wpt/commit/f85428c2c345b9f12856062e303e6dd8c0541095).
Q1 evidence - In #8008 (8a2375a), an omitted `sizes` on a `source` with a lazy `img` parsed as an empty list and resolved to the auto width, without reading the `img`'s `sizes`. #9493 (193c67d) kept this as the note, following https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9448#issuecomment-1623268849, but its parser returned 100vw instead, which this PR fixes. As far as I can tell, inheriting the `img`'s value wasn't discussed. - Chromium [uses `"auto"`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/6ca4e60b94475fa916dfb688608e6cc72693a1bf/third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/html_image_element.cc#L996-L1006). WebKit [uses the `img`'s `sizes`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/15cb3560da6c863025957fce3ee065cf61902e75/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLImageElement.cpp#L324-L325) for any `source` without `sizes`, even when the `img` doesn't allow auto-sizes, since https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/commit/8ef7d8dc0caad77eb47a4189b0a123939429073b. - In "Unrendered img with sizes='auto, 300px' and omitted ``…", Safari TP 255 picks the 300px candidate, while Chrome Canary and Firefox Nightly pick the 100vw one.
Raised elsewhere D1: agammann [noted](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64904#pullrequestreview-5855049395) on web-platform-tests/wpt#64904 that at a fractional DPR the expected candidate's width can round down to just below the DPR. This reproduces in Chrome Canary with `--force-device-scale-factor=1.001`: 2 subtests pick the large candidate. Not applied: [proposed fix](https://github.com/zcorpan/wpt/commit/5bec4d48cd45b4d9ea14eb7b3bc5fa1ef06708b9) rounds the widths up.

> Open: Q1. Not applied: D1. > > New in this review: > > Q1: When a `source` omits `sizes` and the `img` allows auto-sizes, should the `source` use a bare `auto` (as in this PR) or the `img`'s own `sizes` value? They differ when `auto` can't be resolved yet. Take `` before the `img` is rendered; with scripting disabled, it's fetched at that point. A bare `auto` gives 100vw, while the `img`'s value gives 300px. > > * a. Keep as is (bare `auto`). This matches Chromium and Gecko, and what [Add sizes=auto to lazy-loaded  #8008](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/8008) specified and [Force size containment for auto-sizes #9493](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9493)'s note ("equivalent to specifying auto") still says. The `img`'s fallback entries don't apply to the `source`. > * b. Use the `img`'s `sizes` value, so the author's fallback applies when `auto` can't be resolved. This matches WebKit in this case. Prototype: [spec](https://github.com/zcorpan/html/tree/zcorpan/spec-review/html-13211/q1-b), [test](https://github.com/zcorpan/wpt/tree/zcorpan/spec-review/html-13211/q1-b). Option `a` for now to defer behavior changes to a different issue.

For Q1, the fallback values were more intended for legacy UAs than for scripting-disabled cases, though could be useful for both. In non-auto cases though, going with WebKit's approach allows for more DRY markup (when the `sizes` values would have been the same, e.g. if just `type` is different), which seems nice. But yes, this can be decided separately in a follow-up.

Update after review: - **Q1 changed to option b (WebKit behavior).** When a `` has no `sizes` attribute, *update the source set* now uses the following ``'s `sizes` attribute value, if any (170f0302196cd16ba1427d47cc02c893da329caa). This applies whether or not the `img` allows auto-sizes, which matches WebKit's `HTMLImageElement` (`sourceSizesAttr.isNull() ? imgSizesAttr : sourceSizesAttr`). If neither element has `sizes`, the result is still `100vw`. An explicit `` still falls back to `100vw`. The `source` and `img` `sizes` notes were updated to match. - The authoring requirement is unchanged: `` must still be present when the `img` doesn't allow auto-sizes. It could later be relaxed to "when the `img` has no `sizes`". - The PR description should be updated to say *childSizes* is set to the `img`'s `sizes` value, not "auto". - **D1 applied in web-platform-tests/wpt#64904.** Candidate widths are now `Math.ceil`ed, so fractional DPRs no longer land on a density boundary. - **wpt** (b4504a17b019c90608282cca65043ac328abfa8f): the unrendered `sizes="auto, 300px"` case now expects 300px. Added tests for ``, for no `sizes` on either element, and for changing `img.sizes` while the selected `source` has none. Local results for `sizes-auto-parsing.html`: - Safari TP: passes 13/14, including all the omitted-source-sizes tests. The one failure is the non-first bare `auto` recovery case. - Chrome Canary: passes 11/14. All 3 failures are the new inherit-from-img expectations. - Firefox Nightly: still fails the Gecko cases it already failed, plus the new expectations.

No design issues found. Q1 (option b) is applied in 170f030, and I double-checked that it matches [WebKit](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/15cb3560da6c863025957fce3ee065cf61902e75/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLImageElement.cpp#L323-L325): a `source` without `sizes` uses the `img`'s `sizes`, whether or not the `img` allows auto-sizes, and an explicit `sizes=""` still gives 100vw. D1 is applied in https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/commit/3b4a7793f85236fd6d6aa09cab3891e93bfa70bc.
